name: LLVM GlobalISel
listed_description: LLVM instruction selection framework that works on generic Machine IR; the book's quiz answer calls it the best mix of generality and compile-time speed among the three selectors.
claim_text: GlobalISel offers the most flexibility between supporting a wide range of input IR and generating code fast.
book_benchmark: None. Qualitative claim only, no numbers, compiler, flags or CPU stated. Companion repository (PacktPublishing/LLVM-Code-Generation-by-example) holds tutorial backend code, not benchmarks.
found_in: book: LLVM Code Generation (2025), ch. 14 quiz answer 3 (Instruction Selection: Setting Up the Pipeline); also ch. 17 section on register bank selection

name: LLVM FastISel
listed_description: Fast instruction selection sub-framework of SDISel that selects instructions in one pass with no legalization and falls back to SDISel when it cannot handle code; aimed at quick compile time.
book_benchmark: None. This chunk gives no timings; it describes how to wire FastISel into a backend and says it is a sub-selector tried before SDISel.
found_in: book: LLVM Code Generation (2025), ch. 14 section Connecting FastISel to the codegen pipeline; ch. 16 Legalization overview
